proof_interface.strong_local_fields: E_x={Laurent coefficient families bounded below in valuation and tending to zero as exponent tends to minus infinity}; constants K
proof_interface.finite_pole_step: W=P(v_a v'-v_a'v) is constant; residue of (v/v_a)'=W/(P v_a^2) forces W/P'(a)=0, hence v is a constant multiple of v_a and has no negative local coefficients
proof_interface.partial_fraction_step: Strong c0 partial-fraction basis implies no finite negative parts -> v=sum b_j r^j with b_j->0
proof_interface.infinity_step: u1=zF is invertible in E_z; w=v/u1 obeys w'=C/(Pinf F^2), Pinf=4-5z^2+z^4; this kills all negative w coefficients
proof_interface.unbounded_exclusion: U=G/F has U'=1/(2Pinf F^2) and unbounded coefficient norm, so bounded w=c+2CU forces C=0
proof_interface.global_intersection: Global v has only nonpositive z powers from its Tate polynomial part, but K zF has strictly positive powers; therefore v=0
